disease_mechanism_summary: CDD is caused by loss-of-function variants in X-linked CDKL5, a serine/threonine kinase most abundant in brain (EVIDENCE, supportive: MONDO:0100039; UniProt:O76039). Two independent phosphoproteomic studies converge on microtubule regulators MAP1S, EB2 and ARHGEF2 as the physiological substrates; loss of MAP1S phosphorylation leaves MAP1S bound to dendritic microtubules, lengthening growth episodes and impairing dendritic cargo transport, with downstream reduced dendritic arborization, abnormal synapse maturation and altered Akt/rpS6 signalling (EVIDENCE, supportive: PMID:30266824; PMID:30377159). Lowering MAP1S rescues the microtubule-dynamics defect in Cdkl5-null neurons - the field's only clean rescue experiment (EVIDENCE, supportive: PMID:30266824). AAV-delivered CDKL5 raises phospho-EB2 in mouse brain, making pEB2 a quantitative pathway-activity biomarker (EVIDENCE, supportive: PMID:39033321). The decisive uncertainty is the causal chain from lost substrate phosphorylation to the clinical phenotype, above all the infantile pharmacoresistant epilepsy: Cdkl5 knockout mice have no spontaneous seizures, only altered convulsant sensitivity, reduced visual evoked potentials and reduced dendritic complexity (EVIDENCE, contradictory for seizure modelling: PMID:24838000). Human CDD patient-derived guided cortical organoid neurons do show increased firing rate and network synchrony with reduced pEB2, but the phenotype is protocol-dependent and absent in NGN2-induced neurons from the same donors (EVIDENCE, supportive-with-caveat: PMID:40930428). Whether any deficit is reversible after symptom onset is not established in the retrieved literature (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
leverage_points: Phospho-EB2 as a quantitative, in vivo-validated pathway-activity readout that any CDKL5-restoring agent must move, and that any downstream (MAP1S-lowering, excitability) agent must NOT move - giving every arm a built-in specificity control (EVIDENCE: PMID:39033321; PMID:40930428).

MAP1S protein dose as the single node where a genuine rescue has been shown, and whose required perturbation (partial lowering) is exactly what RNase-H gapmer and RNAi pharmacology deliver (EVIDENCE: PMID:30266824).

Visual evoked potential amplitude: a quantitative, translatable, non-seizure efficacy endpoint available today in Cdkl5-null mice and clinically meaningful given cortical visual impairment (EVIDENCE: PMID:24838000).

Human CDD organoid MEA hyperexcitability with isogenic and NGN2 specificity controls - the only retrieved human-tissue functional network phenotype, usable to separate genotype-selective correction from generic firing suppression (EVIDENCE: PMID:40930428).
A dose/duration/mosaic-fraction threshold experiment using transfected CDKL5 mRNA as a research tool, which gates every restoration modality at low cost (INFERENCE from PMID:39033321).
Established intrathecal oligonucleotide dosing in paediatric neurology as a ready delivery route for any transcript-level intervention (EVIDENCE: PMID:34412058).

reviews.why_it_could_work: A published rescue experiment shows that lowering MAP1S normalises microtubule dynamics in Cdkl5-null neurons, and an RNase-H gapmer executes precisely that perturbation - a dose reduction, tunable by ASO dose - in the correct cell type via a clinically validated intrathecal route (EVIDENCE: PMID:30266824; PMID:34412058). Because it acts downstream of the kinase it is genotype-agnostic, covering deletions and truncating alleles that no allele-specific approach can reach (INFERENCE: PMID:30266824).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Mechanistic, not delivery: MAP1S lowering corrects the cell-biological readout while dendritic, VEP and EEG phenotypes stay abnormal because CDKL5 loss acts through parallel substrates (EB2, ARHGEF2) and the Akt/rpS6 axis - pharmacologically successful, therapeutically inert (EVIDENCE, inconclusive: PMID:30266824). Secondary: no safe-lowering window, since MAP1S has CDKL5-independent roles (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied). A negative in vivo result is ambiguous unless regional knockdown is measured in the same animals.
reviews.rationale: The only arm where the dominant failure mode is directly attacked by the proposed experiment. The post-symptomatic ICV gapmer dose-response in Cdkl5-null and wild-type littermates, with mandatory regional MAP1S protein quantification paired to VEP, dendritic arbor and convulsant-threshold EEG, and pEB2 as specificity control, converts the field's one rescue result into an organism-level yes/no and simultaneously tests the postnatal window. Both outcomes are decision-grade: window-positive de-risks a genotype-agnostic target; negative with confirmed deep-cortex knockdown retires MAP1S for all modalities. PURSUE is earned by causal rescue evidence plus a credible, interpretable test - gated behind the in vitro two-genotype window matrix, because an absent window kills it before any chemistry.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The validated rescue was a knockdown, i.e. exactly what RISC does, and CNS siRNA is now a clinically dosable modality (EVIDENCE: PMID:30266824; NCT06393712). Flat, long-duration di-siRNA pharmacology is in principle easier to hold at a partial 30-50% plateau than bolus ASO pharmacology (INFERENCE), which matters because the perturbation must be partial.
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Spatially non-uniform knockdown turning a uniform deficit into a mosaic of opposite cytoskeletal defects: brake release overshoots, so periventricular neurons could be pushed past normal while deep cortex stays untreated, and no chemistry makes RNAi cell-type selective (INFERENCE, contradictory, from the CSF gradient plus PMID:24838000 showing both excitatory and inhibitory populations matter). Compounding this, the mouse has no spontaneous seizures to detect such harm (EVIDENCE, contradictory: PMID:24838000).
reviews.rationale: The two-genotype six-level knockdown matrix is the best experiment per unit cost in this dossier: shared gate for all three MAP1S modalities, no new agent, pre-specified window criterion that can kill the hypothesis. But that experiment is not RNA-specific - it is cell biology - and this arm's own dominant failure mode (in vivo spatial gradient) is untested and arguably worse for RNAi than for a gapmer, where regional PD is easier to titrate. Fund the biology now; keep the RNA implementation behind the oligonucleotide arm. The upstream conclusion of INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE is the right read.

reviews.why_it_could_work: A CNS-penetrant small molecule is the only modality that would reach all forebrain neurons - excitatory, inhibitory, deep and superficial - uniformly, which is precisely the gradient weakness of CSF-delivered oligonucleotides (INFERENCE, supportive). The screening endpoint (microtubule growth-episode length in Cdkl5-null neurons) exists (EVIDENCE: PMID:30266824).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: No ligandable target and no de-risked biology simultaneously. MAP1S has no reported small-molecule binding site, a degrader needs a binder first, and ChEMBL holds no curated mechanism even for CDKL5 (EVIDENCE, contradictory: mcp__rp__chembl_target_drugs (CDKL5)). The validated perturbation is a protein dose reduction, which occupancy pharmacology does not naturally reproduce (INFERENCE, contradictory: PMID:30266824); the non-selective microtubule-stabiliser route has no retrieved CDD data.
reviews.rationale: The upstream analysis correctly refuses to propose a screen and instead proposes gates belonging to other arms - honest, but it means this arm has no experiment that reduces its own uncertainty. Chemistry spend is premature on two independent counts: no in vivo proof-of-concept and no pocket. REJECT as a funding decision today, explicitly reversible: if the genetic gates come back positive, a bounded tractability assessment of the MAP1S-microtubule interface becomes legitimate, and the oral-dosing advantage would then matter. Rejecting the modality is not rejecting the target.

reviews.why_it_could_work: Splice-switching ASOs acting on pre-mRNA in neuronal nuclei after intrathecal dosing are clinically validated, including a patient-specific ASO for an ultra-rare neurological variant, so mechanism, route and an n-of-few regulatory path all exist (EVIDENCE: PMID:34412058). Correction at the endogenous locus yields authentically regulated, correctly localised CDKL5 (INFERENCE: UniProt:O76039), and success is pre-defined quantitatively by restored phospho-EB2 (EVIDENCE: PMID:39033321).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Denominator, not chemistry: the splice-correctable subset of an already ultra-rare disease may be a handful of individuals worldwide, each needing a bespoke ASO with its own toxicology (INFERENCE, contradictory: MONDO:0100039). The generalisable alternative - a CDKL5 poison-exon ASO - currently lacks its essential target, as no non-productive splicing element was retrieved (EVIDENCE, contradictory). Mosaicism caps efficacy in heterozygous females, and no animal carries a human splice variant, so seizure efficacy cannot be tested preclinically (EVIDENCE, contradictory: PMID:24838000).
reviews.rationale: The experiment is well ordered: a near-zero-cost in silico variant classification counting candidate splice-correctable individuals against a pre-set go/no-go threshold, before any bench spend, then ASO tiling on patient neurons or a minigene with gymnotic uptake and pEB2 readout. That attacks the dominant failure mode first. I withhold PURSUE because the biology being restored is certain while the population may not exist, and because reversibility after symptom onset is unresolved - a splice ASO delivered after infantile seizure onset may arrive too late. Fund Stage 1 and the long-read poison-exon check; keep the tiling protocol as a dormant, triggerable n-of-1 capability rather than a programme.

reviews.why_it_could_work: CDKL5 is a catalytic protein, so sub-stoichiometric restoration may suffice, and exogenously supplied CDKL5 is demonstrably functional in brain as judged by raised phospho-EB2 (EVIDENCE: PMID:39033321; INFERENCE: UniProt:O76039).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: No vehicle plus a pharmacokinetic mismatch. No neuron-tropic LNP exists at clinical maturity; CSF-administered LNPs transfect ependyma, meninges and glia far more readily than deep parenchymal postmitotic neurons (EVIDENCE/INFERENCE, contradictory). The specific danger is silent failure: bulk-tissue pEB2 reading as success from non-neuronal cells while the disease-driving neurons are untransfected. mRNA also gives days of protein against a lifelong developmental requirement, and chronic repeat intrathecal LNP dosing in infants has no safety precedent.
reviews.rationale: REJECT the therapeutic arm - the upstream conclusion of NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH is correct, and an attractive mechanism must not outrank a non-existent vehicle. But the re-scoping is the most valuable single contribution here and should be funded under a different heading: CDKL5 mRNA as a research tool to establish how much protein, in what fraction of neurons, for how long, is enough (dose-response against pEB2 and dendritic arbor; pulse versus repeated pulse; mixed-genotype co-cultures at defined ratios), plus the dominant-negative co-expression test classifying patient missense alleles. Those readouts gate the oligonucleotide and small-molecule output-boost arms and resolve two named major unknowns. Reject as a therapy, fund as a tool.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The only output-boost implementation with an agent already given to CDD patients: ataluren completed Phase 2 in CDKL5 and Dravet nonsense variants, so systemic tolerability in this population has been explored and a clinical path exists (EVIDENCE: NCT02758626). Oral CNS-penetrant molecules reach the mosaic mutant-expressing neuronal subset uniformly (INFERENCE), and mosaicism means modest percentage gains could move many cells above threshold - a profile that fits low-efficiency readthrough better than an all-or-nothing requirement (INFERENCE: MONDO:0100039).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Readthrough: neuronal efficiency is typically low single-digit percent and codon-context dependent, so full-length CDKL5 may never cross threshold; ataluren's CNS exposure and neuronal readthrough efficiency were not retrieved and the completed trial yielded no therapy (EVIDENCE, contradictory: NCT02758626 - outcome not retrieved, so suggestive rather than proof of failure). Chaperoning: no CDKL5 stabiliser or curated mechanism exists (EVIDENCE: mcp__rp__chembl_target_drugs (CDKL5)), an ATP-site ligand risks inhibiting the kinase it stabilises, and if kinase-domain missense alleles are dominant-negative, stabilisation increases a harmful species (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
reviews.rationale: The dominant-negative co-expression test - express each patient missense allele in CDKL5-null neurons, then ask whether it suppresses wild-type-driven pEB2 - can kill the chaperone arm before any screening spend and resolves a named major unknown. That is a textbook cheap disqualifying experiment and should be funded. The readthrough arm is interpretable only against a pre-specified pEB2 threshold, which is why it must run alongside the mRNA-tool dose-response. INVESTIGATE not PURSUE: a drug has already been through this population without producing a therapy, the addressable subset is small, deletions are unaddressable, and the direction of effect for missense stabilisation is unknown. Do not restart a clinical readthrough attempt before the neuronal pEB2 data exist.

reviews.why_it_could_work: Akt/rpS6 signalling is measurably altered in Cdkl5 knockout mice, and because that axis sits immediately downstream of cell-surface growth-factor receptors, a secreted ligand or receptor agonist is formally the only biologic class that could engage it without intracellular delivery (EVIDENCE: PMID:24838000; INFERENCE). Quantitative non-seizure endpoints (VEP, dendritic morphology) exist.
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Target definition collapsing into delivery impossibility. The perturbation wanted - continuous, uniform, dendrite-level modulation of essentially every forebrain neuron from infancy - is the hardest biologic delivery problem there is; antibodies cross an intact BBB at fractions of a percent of plasma level, and intrathecal dosing favours ependyma and superficial cortex (INFERENCE, contradictory). No cell-surface receptor node has been nominated in CDD because the chain from lost substrate phosphorylation to epilepsy is unestablished (EVIDENCE, inconclusive: PMID:30266824). No biologic has entered CDD development at all (EVIDENCE: NCT03572933, NCT03861871, NCT03694275, NCT05626634).
reviews.rationale: REJECT the programme, accept the probe. Opening a biologic effort would mean years of BBB-shuttle engineering for a target never shown to be right - a clear case of a good-sounding mechanism outranking missing delivery. The proposed bounded target-nomination experiment is nonetheless sound and nearly free: add IGF-1, an IGF-1-derived peptide, BDNF and a control growth factor to the organoid MEA panel already being run, testing the genotype x ligand interaction on phospho-rpS6/phospho-Akt and on firing and synchrony, with pEB2 as expected-unchanged control. This pre-registers the single condition under which a CDD biologic should ever be opened, for a few extra wells. Even a positive result only earns a delivery feasibility assessment and a head-to-head against a CNS-penetrant small molecule at the same node.

reviews.why_it_could_work: The only CDD hypothesis with approved and clinical-stage chemical matter and demonstrated brain exposure in this exact population: ganaxolone completed a randomised Phase 3 in CDD, fenfluramine advanced from Phase 2 to an active Phase 3, bexicaserin and soticlestat have been dosed in CDD/DEE (EVIDENCE: NCT03572933; NCT03861871, NCT05064878; NCT05626634; NCT03694275). Delivery is solved and the route is genotype-agnostic. A human-tissue phenotype now exists to test against: CDD patient organoid cortical neurons show increased firing and synchrony with reduced pEB2, letting target engagement and therapeutic readout be dissociated in one assay (EVIDENCE: PMID:40930428).
reviews.dominant_failure_mode: Mechanism-blind repurposing with a demonstrated ceiling. The chain from substrate hypophosphorylation to epilepsy is unestablished, so no CDD-specific target can be named and existing agents are symptomatic (EVIDENCE, inconclusive: PMID:30266824). Seizures are pharmacoresistant by definition and available drugs reduce rather than abolish them (INFERENCE, contradictory: MONDO:0100039). Soticlestat's rare-epilepsy study was terminated after negative Phase 3 SKYLINE/SKYWAY results (EVIDENCE, contradictory: NCT03635073). Knockout mice have no spontaneous seizures, so the primary clinical endpoint is unmodellable (EVIDENCE, contradictory: PMID:24838000).
reviews.rationale: The experiment is unusually well specified because it makes the genotype x drug interaction the primary analysis rather than the main effect of drug - that single design choice separates disease modification from generic dampening, and it is the question the clinical programmes never asked. The NGN2 arm from the same donors is a real built-in negative control, and including an Akt/rpS6 probe in each direction resolves the unspecified direction of correction. I stop short of PURSUE: the organoid phenotype is protocol-dependent and absent in NGN2 neurons from the same patients, it is developmental tissue lacking mature glia and X-inactivation mosaicism, and may not model established pharmacoresistant epilepsy - so the experiment partly validates the assay while using it. Fund it; do not fund another Phase 2 signal-seeking study on an existing excitability mechanism until a genotype-selective interaction is shown.

comparative_judgment: Three hypotheses, but only one rests on a rescue experiment, and that asymmetry should drive allocation. MAP1S-brake release is the only arm where a published manipulation reversed a disease phenotype in disease-genotype cells (PMID:30266824), and its required perturbation - partial protein dose reduction - maps cleanly onto one modality class. Within that hypothesis the modalities are not interchangeable. The oligonucleotide gapmer wins over RNAi for the same target for a non-obvious reason: the arm's in vivo risk is a spatial gradient of knockdown, and because brake release overshoots rather than merely under-treating, a gradient can be actively harmful; bolus gapmer pharmacology makes regional PD easier to titrate and measure, which is what makes a negative result interpretable. Durable di-siRNA becomes the better chronic implementation only after the window and gradient questions are answered. The small-molecule version is rejected on two independent grounds (no pocket, no in vivo proof-of-concept) while keeping its one genuine advantage - uniform forebrain access - on the table for later. All three MAP1S modalities share a single cheap gate, the two-genotype graded knockdown matrix; if no window exists, no delivery chemistry saves any of them, so that experiment precedes modality-specific spend. CDKL5 output boost has the most certain biology - raising functional CDKL5 is unambiguously the right direction, with pEB2 as a quantitative success criterion (PMID:39033321) - and the weakest denominator. The modality comparison is stark: the splice-switching oligonucleotide has a real mechanism, route and n-of-few precedent (PMID:34412058) but may have almost no eligible patients; the small molecule has an agent already dosed in CDD (NCT02758626) but low expected readthrough efficiency and, for the chaperone branch, an unresolved direction of effect that could make the intervention harmful; the RNA implementation is rejected outright because the vehicle does not exist and its failure would be silent, with bulk pEB2 reading positive from ependyma while the driving neurons are untouched. The right move is to spend almost nothing on chemistry and buy two shared gating datasets: the in silico variant-class count (does a splice-correctable population exist?) and the variant-function catalogue with the dominant-negative co-expression test (which alleles are hypomorphic, and is stabilisation safe?). Both can kill expensive programmes for the cost of weeks. E/I rebalance inverts the pattern: best delivery, the only approved CDD drug, worst mechanistic specification. Its small-molecule arm is worth funding not to find another anti-seizure medicine - soticlestat's negative Phase 3 (NCT03635073) and CDD pharmacoresistance (MONDO:0100039) show that ceiling - but because the genotype x drug interaction design asks whether any excitability mechanism is CDD-selective, the question that distinguishes disease modification from symptom suppression. Its protein arm is the clearest reject: the perturbation wanted is continuous dendrite-level modulation of every forebrain neuron from infancy, exactly what biologics cannot deliver, and no surface receptor has been nominated; it survives only as a few extra wells of ligand probe inside the organoid experiment. Across hypotheses, the most under-appreciated cross-cutting gap is reversibility and timing. Nothing retrieved shows that restoring CDKL5 or correcting its downstream node after symptom onset improves anything, and CDD seizures begin in the first months of life. Every strategy here is bounded by that unknown, which is why the MAP1S in vivo study should be dosed post-symptomatically rather than neonatally - a design choice that buys window information at no extra cost. What would change my mind: a positive post-symptomatic MAP1S in vivo result with confirmed deep-cortex PD would move that arm to a lead-optimisation commitment and make the small-molecule tractability question worth asking; a confirmed-PD negative would retire MAP1S across all modalities and shift everything to CDKL5-level restoration and circuit work. Demonstration of a genuine non-productive splicing element in human neuronal CDKL5 transcripts would transform the splice-ASO arm from n-of-1 capability into a generalisable programme and likely make it the highest-value arm here. A genotype-selective interaction for any already-dosed excitability drug would justify a CDD-specific clinical hypothesis with VEP as a non-seizure pharmacodynamic endpoint. And a seizure-competent CDD model with spontaneous seizures would change the calculus for every arm, because at present no approach here can be tested against the endpoint families care about most.
what_is_known: EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID:30266824): lowering MAP1S rescued abnormal microtubule dynamics in Cdkl5 knockout neurons, and EB2 phosphorylation is reduced in patient-derived neurons. The field's only clean rescue and the sole causal anchor for a downstream target.

EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID:30377159): two independent phosphoproteomic studies converge on microtubule regulators (MAP1S, EB2, ARHGEF2) as the physiological CDKL5 substrates - convergence, not single-study association.

EVIDENCE (supportive, PMID:39033321): restoring CDKL5 to mouse brain raises phospho-EB2, establishing pEB2 as a quantitative pathway-activity biomarker and a pre-defined success criterion for output-boosting agents.

EVIDENCE (contradictory for the key endpoint, PMID:24838000): Cdkl5 knockout mice have no spontaneous seizures - only altered convulsant sensitivity - alongside reduced VEPs, reduced dendritic arborization and altered Akt/rpS6 signalling; distinct behaviours map to excitatory versus inhibitory forebrain neurons. The primary clinical endpoint is unmodellable in the standard mouse.

EVIDENCE (supportive with caveat, PMID:40930428): CDD patient-derived guided cortical organoid neurons show increased weighted mean firing rate and network synchrony with reduced pEB2, but NGN2-induced neurons from the same donors show no MEA or neurite phenotype - a usable human assay with a fragile, protocol-dependent window.

EVIDENCE (NCT03572933; NCT03861871, NCT05064878; NCT05626634; NCT03694275): the E/I route has already produced clinically deployed and clinical-stage CDD therapies, so CNS exposure and tolerability in this population are established.
EVIDENCE (contradictory, NCT03635073): soticlestat's rare-epilepsy study was terminated after negative Phase 3 SKYLINE/SKYWAY results - a plausible excitability-lowering drug failing at scale in DEE.

EVIDENCE (contradictory, NCT02758626): ataluren, the readthrough implementation of the output-boost hypothesis, completed Phase 2 in CDKL5/Dravet nonsense variants without yielding a CDD therapy. Outcome not retrieved, so suggestive, not proof of failure.

EVIDENCE (PMID:34412058): intrathecal splice-modulating and transcript-lowering oligonucleotides are clinically validated in paediatric neurological disease, including a patient-specific ASO for an ultra-rare variant - route and n-of-few regulatory path exist.

EVIDENCE (contradictory, mcp__rp__chembl_target_drugs (CDKL5)): no curated drug mechanism exists for CDKL5 and no MAP1S-directed or CDKL5-stabilising chemical matter was identified - these nodes are chemically unexplored.

EVIDENCE (contradictory, none retrieved): no neuron-tropic LNP or CNS mRNA agent in clinical development; no validated non-productive splicing element in CDKL5; no Map1s/Cdkl5 double-mutant animal; no biologic in CDD development.
critical_gaps: Does partial MAP1S lowering produce any organism-level benefit in Cdkl5-null mice, and is there a therapeutic window at all - a knockdown depth that corrects null neurons while leaving wild-type neurons normal? Untested; blocks every MAP1S modality (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

Reversibility and timing: no retrieved evidence that restoring CDKL5 or correcting its downstream node after symptom onset improves anything. CDD seizures begin in the first months of life, so this bounds every strategy (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

How much CDKL5 protein, in what fraction of neurons, for how long, is enough to normalise pEB2 and dendritic phenotypes - the threshold that makes readthrough, splice-correction and any partial-restoration result interpretable (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
Are kinase-domain missense variants hypomorphic, null or dominant-negative? If dominant-negative, stabilisation increases a harmful species and that arm must not start (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

What fraction of reported CDKL5 alleles is genuinely output-limited and splice-correctable, and does a CDKL5 non-productive splicing element exist that would make an output-boost ASO generalisable rather than bespoke (EVIDENCE, contradictory: none retrieved).

No seizure-competent CDD model with spontaneous seizures was identified, so the endpoint that matters most to families cannot be interrogated preclinically by any approach in this dossier (EVIDENCE, contradictory: PMID:24838000).
Which neuron subtype and which developmental window generate the epileptic phenotype - without this, no CDD-specific excitability target can be named (EVIDENCE, inconclusive: PMID:30266824).

next_actions.action: Two-genotype graded Map1s knockdown matrix: titrate Map1s siRNA to ~0/15/30/50/70/90% protein reduction (quantified per condition) in paired Cdkl5-null and wild-type primary cortical/hippocampal neurons, non-targeting siRNA at matched load; read microtubule growth-episode length (EB3 comets), dendritic cargo transport and dendritic arbor complexity; overlay both genotype dose-response curves. Repeat in CDKL5 patient-derived neurons if available.
next_actions.question_answered: Does a therapeutic window exist for MAP1S lowering at all - a depth that normalises Cdkl5-null neurons while leaving wild-type neurons unaffected?
next_actions.activity_required: Paired primary neuron cultures, siRNA titration with per-condition MAP1S quantification, live imaging; no new agent needed. Weeks, low cost.
next_actions.supports_if: At least one knockdown level makes null neurons indistinguishable from untreated wild-type on both microtubule and dendritic readouts while wild-type neurons at that same level are also unaffected - a defined window that becomes the design specification for all MAP1S modalities.
next_actions.kills_if: Wild-type curves degrade at or below the depth that corrects null neurons (no window), or null dendritic arborization fails to improve at any depth despite corrected microtubule dynamics. Either outcome stops MAP1S lowering across oligonucleotide, RNA and small-molecule arms - no delivery chemistry rescues a mechanism with no window.

next_actions.action: In silico CDKL5 variant-class census: classify all reported CDKL5 variants in public variant and registry datasets into deletion / frameshift / nonsense / missense / splice-region / deep-intronic, flagging splice-class alleles predicted to create cryptic sites or pseudoexons with retained partial normal splicing; output a count of candidate splice-correctable individuals against a pre-set go/no-go threshold. In parallel, a bounded long-read/RNA-seq check for a non-productive splicing element in human neuronal CDKL5 transcripts.
next_actions.question_answered: Does a denominator exist for a CDKL5 splice-switching ASO, and is there a poison-exon element that would make an output-boost ASO generalisable instead of bespoke?
next_actions.activity_required: Database analysis, essentially no bench cost; plus one long-read sequencing experiment on human neuronal CDKL5 transcripts.
next_actions.supports_if: A splice-correctable cohort of meaningful size (tens, not single digits) is identified, and/or a non-productive CDKL5 splicing element is demonstrated - the latter converting this into a generalisable programme serving all patients with one intact allele.
next_actions.kills_if: The splice-correctable set is a handful of individuals worldwide and no non-productive element exists. Then stop the generalisable splice-ASO programme and retain the tiling protocol only as a dormant, on-demand n-of-1 capability triggered by a qualifying patient plus a sponsor.

next_actions.action: Variant-function catalogue with dominant-negative test: express patient kinase-domain missense alleles in CDKL5-null neurons and measure phospho-EB2 to classify each as null or hypomorphic; then co-express each with wild-type CDKL5 and test whether it suppresses wild-type-driven pEB2. For hypomorphic non-suppressing alleles, distinguish destabilised from catalytically dead (cycloheximide chase plus activity-per-unit-protein). Run alongside a dose/duration/mosaic-fraction titration using chemically modified CDKL5 mRNA as a tool reagent (graded dose versus pEB2 and dendritic arbor; single versus repeated pulse; mixed transfected/untransfected co-cultures at 10/25/50/75%).
next_actions.question_answered: Is stabilising mutant CDKL5 safe or harmful, and how much CDKL5 protein, in what fraction of neurons, for how long, is enough? This is the shared threshold that makes every restoration result interpretable.
next_actions.activity_required: Cdkl5-null and patient-derived iPSC cortical neurons, mRNA/plasmid expression, quantitative pEB2 immunoassay, MEA for network readouts. No new chemistry.
next_actions.supports_if: A meaningful set of alleles is hypomorphic, destabilised and non-suppressing (legitimate chaperone targets), and a clear restoration threshold emerges - e.g. partial restoration in a minority of neurons normalises pEB2 and dendritic metrics, with benefit persisting beyond the protein's presence. This lowers the bar for every restoration modality and justifies the in vivo timing study.
next_actions.kills_if: Missense alleles are predominantly catalytically dead or dominant-negative - then do not start chaperone chemistry at all. Or phenotypes require near-complete, continuous CDKL5 in nearly all neurons with strictly cell-autonomous correction - then abandon transient-expression modalities and down-weight anything that cannot achieve broad sustained pan-neuronal correction.

next_actions.action: Post-symptomatic ICV gapmer study (gated on action 1 showing a window): single ICV bolus dose-response of a validated Map1s gapmer (3 doses) versus control oligonucleotide in Cdkl5-null and wild-type littermates, dosed at ~P30-P45 rather than neonatally. Four weeks later, in the same animals: regional MAP1S protein in superficial cortex, deep cortex and hippocampus (mandatory); phospho-EB2 as specificity control; VEP amplitude; convulsant-threshold EEG; sparse-label dendritic arbor quantification in visual and somatosensory cortex.
next_actions.question_answered: Does partial MAP1S lowering convert the microtubule-dynamics rescue into organism-level benefit, and does it still work after phenotype onset (the postnatal window question that bounds all approaches)?
next_actions.activity_required: Gapmer synthesis and validation, ICV dosing, regional PD immunoassay, electrophysiology (VEP, convulsant EEG), histology. The regional PD measurement is non-negotiable - without it a negative result is uninterpretable.
next_actions.supports_if: In regions where MAP1S is lowered 30-60%, VEP amplitude and/or dendritic complexity shift significantly toward wild-type with a dose-response, wild-type animals at the same exposure are unchanged, and pEB2 stays low - confirming the effect is downstream of the kinase rather than off-target CDKL5 restoration. Commit to lead optimisation and chronic tolerability.
next_actions.kills_if: Verified 40-60% MAP1S lowering in deep cortex and hippocampus with no movement in VEP, dendritic arbor or convulsant threshold - or benefit only at doses that degrade wild-type animals. Stop the MAP1S arm for all modalities. If deep PD is poor, the question is delivery not biology: repeat with conditional genetic Map1s reduction before further chemistry spend.

next_actions.action: Genotype x drug organoid MEA study: record CDD patient-derived guided cortical organoid neurons versus isogenic controls across the early window where hyperexcitability is present, testing concentration-response panels of the clinically precedented CDD mechanisms (ganaxolone, fenfluramine, bexicaserin, soticlestat) plus an Akt/rpS6 probe in each direction, plus a few wells of extracellular ligands (IGF-1, IGF-1-derived peptide, BDNF, control growth factor) as the biologic target-nomination probe. Primary analysis is the genotype x drug interaction on firing rate and synchrony, not the main effect of drug; measure pEB2 and phospho-rpS6 at endpoint; run the identical panel in NGN2 neurons from the same donors as a phenotype-null specificity arm.
next_actions.question_answered: Is any excitability or growth-factor mechanism CDD-selective - correcting mutant networks toward control - or does it merely dampen firing equally in mutant and control neurons? This separates disease modification from the demonstrated symptomatic ceiling and pre-registers the only condition under which a CDD biologic should be opened.
next_actions.activity_required: CDD and isogenic organoid cultures plus donor-matched NGN2 neurons, MEA recording, concentration-response panels, pEB2/phospho-rpS6 immunoassay. Marginal extra cost for the ligand probe arm.
next_actions.supports_if: At least one mechanism produces significant genotype-selective normalisation - mutant firing/synchrony returns toward control at a concentration leaving control networks largely unaffected, absent in the NGN2 arm, ideally with phospho-rpS6 correction - and on follow-up the same agent raises convulsant threshold and increases VEP amplitude in Cdkl5-null mice. For an already-dosed drug this justifies a CDD-specific clinical hypothesis with VEP as a non-seizure pharmacodynamic endpoint.
next_actions.kills_if: All agents suppress firing similarly in mutant and control networks (main effect, no interaction), or correct firing in vitro with no VEP improvement in vivo. Retire mechanism-blind repurposing here and redirect spend to identifying the neuron subtype and developmental window generating the epileptic phenotype and to building a seizure-competent CDD model. Either outcome also validates or kills the organoid MEA platform as the field's screening assay.

do_not_fund_yet: Any MAP1S-directed small-molecule or degrader hit-finding. MAP1S has no reported binding site, a degrader needs a binder first, and ChEMBL holds no curated mechanism even for CDKL5 (EVIDENCE: mcp__rp__chembl_target_drugs (CDKL5)). The target is simultaneously unligandable and un-de-risked in vivo; chemistry must stay gated behind the genetic window matrix and the ICV gapmer result.

The non-selective brain-penetrant microtubule-stabiliser route (epothilone-class) for this node. No CDD-context data was retrieved and the mechanism cannot deliver selective MAP1S occupancy reduction (EVIDENCE, contradictory: none retrieved).

CNS siRNA/di-siRNA chemistry and delivery development for MAP1S before the in vitro window is defined and before the in vivo gradient question is answered with a gapmer, where regional PD is easier to titrate. If no window exists, no delivery chemistry helps (INFERENCE from PMID:30266824).

Any CDKL5 mRNA/LNP therapeutic programme. No neuron-tropic LNP exists at clinical maturity, CSF-delivered LNPs favour ependyma and meninges over deep neurons, and mRNA's days-long protein supply is mismatched to a lifelong developmental requirement. The specific hazard is silent failure in which bulk-tissue pEB2 reads positive from non-neuronal cells (EVIDENCE/INFERENCE, contradictory: none retrieved). Fund the mRNA only as a dose/duration/mosaic tool reagent.

A CDKL5 poison-exon ASO programme. Its essential target - a non-productive splicing element in CDKL5 - was not established in retrieved evidence and must be demonstrated by long-read/RNA-seq first (EVIDENCE, contradictory: none retrieved).

Bespoke per-patient splice-ASO toxicology packages before the variant-class census shows a cohort above a pre-set threshold. The dominant failure mode here is denominator, not chemistry (INFERENCE, contradictory: MONDO:0100039).

A CDKL5 chaperone/stabiliser screening campaign before the dominant-negative co-expression test. If kinase-domain missense alleles are dominant-negative, stabilisation would increase a harmful species (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).

A renewed clinical readthrough attempt in CDD. Ataluren already completed Phase 2 in CDKL5 nonsense variants without producing a therapy, and its neuronal CNS exposure and readthrough efficiency are unknown; neuronal pEB2 data against a pre-specified threshold must come first (EVIDENCE, contradictory: NCT02758626).

Any biologic programme for CDD, including BBB-shuttle engineering. No cell-surface node has been nominated, the chain from substrate hypophosphorylation to epilepsy is unestablished, and the perturbation wanted is the hardest biologic delivery problem there is (EVIDENCE, inconclusive: PMID:30266824; INFERENCE, contradictory). Allow only the few-well ligand probe inside the organoid experiment.

Another Phase 2 signal-seeking trial of an existing excitability mechanism in CDD. Seizures are pharmacoresistant by definition and soticlestat's negative Phase 3 shows the ceiling; fund the genotype x drug interaction test instead (INFERENCE: MONDO:0100039; EVIDENCE: NCT03635073).

Any programme whose value depends on post-symptomatic reversibility, until the timing question is addressed - which is why the in vivo MAP1S study should be dosed post-symptomatically rather than neonatally (HYPOTHESIS, not_studied).
conclusion_note: Decision support for researchers, not medical advice. The cause of CDD is certain and one genuine rescue experiment exists (MAP1S lowering, PMID:30266824), so the disease can be responsibly planned - but every arm is bounded by two unresolved questions: whether deficits are reversible after symptom onset, and how the substrate defect causes epilepsy. No seizure-competent CDD model was identified, so the endpoint families care about most cannot currently be tested by any approach here. Upstream retrieval was incomplete (some PubMed searches returned HTTP 429), and several key claims rest on absence of retrieved agents, which in an ultra-rare disease is weak negative evidence.
